title: Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence in the German Software Engineering Industry: An Empirical Study.
verified_bounded_claim: Adoption and perceived productivity vary with experience, organizational size, interaction depth, regulatory constraints, and available project context.
verification_note: The mixed-methods sample is German and self-reported; carry those population and measurement boundaries into any manuscript use.

title: A Preliminary Study of Multilingual Code Language Models for Code Generation Task Using Translated Benchmarks.
verified_bounded_claim: Translated benchmarks preserve useful multilingual evaluation signals while producing cross-benchmark inconsistencies and reproducibility constraints.
verification_note: This is a preliminary study with explicit hardware, model-size, and language-coverage limits.

title: PPM: Automated Generation of Diverse Programming Problems for Benchmarking Code Generation Models.
verified_bounded_claim: Benchmark generation should test semantic diversity and contamination risk rather than relying only on homogeneous perturbations.
verification_note: The paper evaluates two PPM implementations against named baselines; use its results within those benchmark and model conditions.

title: The Patch Overfitting Problem in Automated Program Repair: Practical Magnitude and a Baseline for Realistic Benchmarking.
verified_bounded_claim: Patch-overfitting magnitude varies by tool and bug in the studied Defects4J workload; assessment techniques should be compared with the paper's random-selection baseline.
verification_note: The empirical result covers ten APR tools, Defects4J 1.5, and a three-hour execution boundary.

title: COFFE: A Code Efficiency Benchmark for Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: Correctness benchmarks can miss execution efficiency; COFFE uses discriminating stress tests and CPU instruction counts to make efficiency comparison more stable.
verification_note: The paper focuses on function- and file-level generation and states platform and validity limits; it does not establish a universal cost metric.

title: Causality-Aided Evaluation and Explanation of Large Language Model-Based Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: The method augments outcome evaluation with a causal-graph analysis of prompt-code relationships and reports actionable prompt-calibration insights subject to stated validity threats.
verification_note: The accessible preprint has an earlier title and studies three models; verify final-version counts before using details unique to the DOI article.

title: The First Prompt Counts the Most! An Evaluation of Large Language Models on Iterative Example-Based Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: In the evaluated iterative example-based tasks, successful functionality implementation was concentrated in early rounds and depended strongly on the initial examples.
verification_note: The result is specific to six evaluated models, 172 target functionalities, and the paper's I/O-example protocol.

title: Poracle: Testing Patches under Preservation Conditions to Combat the Overfitting Problem of Program Repair.
verified_bounded_claim: Patch assessment can combine user-specified preservation conditions with differential fuzzing to find behavior regressions beyond the original bug-triggering tests.
verification_note: The method assumes deterministic programs for the relevant inputs and requires a human to specify the preservation condition.

title: Benchmarking and Categorizing the Performance of Neural Program Repair Systems for Java.
verified_bounded_claim: Comparative neural-repair evaluation benefits from unified training data and bug-type performance categories instead of aggregate fixed-bug counts alone.
verification_note: The benchmark evaluates nine Java NPR systems; its categories and performance results should not be generalized to other repair families without new evidence.

title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Neural Program Repair with Natural Robustness Testing.
verified_bounded_claim: Neural-repair evaluations should distinguish naturally occurring semantic-preserving transformations and measure robustness under those variations rather than rely only on the nominal dataset.
verification_note: The naturalness study and transformation set are bounded; the reported prediction and patch-rate changes do not establish all real-world variations.

title: MultiPL-E: A Scalable and Polyglot Approach to Benchmarking Neural Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: Polyglot benchmark translation broadens language coverage while making compiler translation, prompt validity, and per-language execution part of the measurement contract.
verification_note: The benchmark translates two Python suites into 18 additional languages and documents translation and execution limitations.

title: Correlating Automated and Human Evaluation of Code Documentation Generation Quality.
verified_bounded_claim: Automated documentation metrics require direct comparison with human judgments before being used as quality proxies; in this study they were not reliable substitutes for human evaluation.
verification_note: The findings concern the studied code-comment and commit-message tasks, metrics, models, and annotator protocol.

title: The impact of human factors on the participation decision of reviewers in modern code review.
verified_bounded_claim: Reviewer participation in the four studied systems was associated with human and experience factors, especially prior participation rate and code-authoring experience.
verification_note: This observational case study reports associations, not causal effects, across Android, LibreOffice, OpenStack, and Qt.

title: An Empirical Investigation of Relevant Changes and Automation Needs in Modern Code Review.
verified_bounded_claim: Developers in the study distinguished code-review tasks that were difficult to automate from tasks such as license-header generation that could receive automated support.
verification_note: The evidence is survey- and taxonomy-based and should retain the paper's participant and task boundaries.

title: Support, Not Automation: Towards AI-supported Code Review For Code Quality and Beyond.
verified_bounded_claim: The paper argues that code review is associated with interpersonal and team benefits and proposes AI support intended to preserve those functions.
verification_note: The institutional repository identifies this copy as a peer-reviewed post-print. The paper advances a position and research agenda; it does not estimate the effect of a deployed support intervention.

title: HalluJudge: A Reference-Free Hallucination Detection for Context Misalignment in Code Review Automation.
verified_bounded_claim: Reference-free context-alignment judgments showed measurable detection performance, per-assessment cost, and partial alignment with developer preference in the studied enterprise setting.
verification_note: The results use proprietary Atlassian data and specified judge models; treat the reported F1, cost, and preference alignment as setting-specific.

title: Cognitive Biases in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study.
verified_bounded_claim: Software-engineering studies document numerous cognitive biases, while the mapped debiasing proposals covered few biases and lacked strong empirical effectiveness evidence.
verification_note: The mapping covers literature through 2016 and explicitly separates documented bias research from untested debiasing suggestions.

title: Logging Practices in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study.
verified_bounded_claim: Logging research documents recurring implementation problems and low industry uptake of proposed solutions, supporting operational validation of observability protocols.
verification_note: The paper frames current logging practice as arbitrary or ad hoc and maps 56 primary studies. Treat this as a secondary-review observation, not a direct prevalence estimate.
